name: October 21, 2025 Regular Meeting
minutes_text:
MINUTES
  PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  OCTOBER 21, 2025
  MULTIPURPOSE ROOM
  6:30 P.M.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Chair Villablanca called the meeting to order at 6:36 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Chair Judy Villablanca; Commissioners Alicia Peak (arrived at 6:43 p.m.),
  Georgia Goldfarb, and Dane Skophammer

  ABSENT: Vice Chair Jake Lingo

  ALSO PRESENT: Kristin Riesgo, Community Services Director; Chris Orosz, Interim
  Recreation Manager; and Brittany Saleaumua, Administrative Assistant

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Chair Villablanca led the Pledge of Allegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Skophammer moved, and Commissioner Goldbfarb seconded a
  motion to approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried 3—
  0; Vice Chair Lingo and Commissioner Peak absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Administrative Assistant Saleaumua reported the agenda for the meeting was
  posted on October 16, 2025.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC

  Chair Villablanca closed public comment.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  Commissioner Goldfarb moved, and Chair Villablanca seconded a motion to
  approve the consent calendar. The question was called, and the motion carried 3-0;
  Vice Chair Lingo and Commissioner Peak absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  A.  PreviouslV Discussed Items
  None.
  B.  New Items
  I.  Approval of Minutes
  Recommended Action: Approve the minutes for the August 19, 2025 Parks
  and Recreation Commission Regular meeting.
  2.  Community Services Department Monthlv Report
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report of activities, events,
  projects, and programs coordinated by the Community Services Department
  in September 2025.

  Commissioner Peak arrived at 6:43 pm.

ITEM 4  OLD BUSINESS

  None.

ITEM 5  NEW BUSINESS

  Legacy Park Rehabilitation Proiect and Program Update
  Recommended Action: Receive and file a report on the Legacy Park rehabilitation
  proj ect and outreach programs.

  Interim Recreation Manager Orosz presented the staff report.

  Commissioner Goldfarb stated the impact of plant biodiversity on human health
  had been studied.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Interim Recreation Manager Orosz stated staff
  were reviewing options to add a pollinator garden at Malibu Bluffs Park.

  In response to Commissioner Goldfarb, Interim Recreation Manager Orosz stated
  the Department of Fire and Forestry Protection would assist at the November plant
  giveaway, and the Pollinator Protection Fund would assist with the spring plant
  giveaway.

  Commissioner Peak stated Legacy Park field trips could be provided for Webster
  Elementary School.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated staff were working with the Lost Hills Sheriffs Department to add language
  to the "No Camping" signs at Legacy Park.

  Chair Villablanca supported hiring security guards at Legacy Park to assist with
  enforcement.

  Park Enhancement and Donation Program
  Recommended Action: l) Review and discuss recommended revisions to the Park
  Enhancement and Donation Program; and 2) Recommend City Council approve the
  revisions to the program.

  Community Services Director Riesgo presented the staff report.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  Charmlee Wilderness Park was managed by the Mountains Recreation and
  Conservation Authority in 2018 when the Commission previously reviewed the
  Park Enhancement and Donation Program. She stated the Commission should
  consider adding Charmlee Wilderness Park to the donation acceptance list.

  In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo
  stated the Skate Park had various location options for a memorial donation.

  Chair Villablanca stated she supported adding new tiles to the Skate Park for
  memorial options, and she did not want memorial items in the skate area.

MOTION  Chair Villablanca moved, and Commissioner Peak seconded a motion to include
  Charmlee Wilderness Park and the Skate Park to the list of acceptable locations for
  the Park Enhancement and Donation Program. The question was called, and the
  motion carried 4—0; Vice Chair Lingo absent.

  Chair Villablanca stated families would be upset if a donated item was removed
  from the park without prior notice.

  Commissioner Skophammer stated the City contract includes language that
  guarantees memorial items would be kept intact for seven years, and it would be
  unfair not to give donors the right of refusal if the City planned to remove the
  memorial item. He stated the City could require an additional monetary donation to
  keep the item at the park.

  In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
  that the original donors did not sign an agreement acknowledging that the memorial
  items would remain intact for seven years and could potentially be removed
  afterward.

Commissioner Skophammer stated there should be a vetting process or a time limit
on park memorial items.

Commissioner Peak indicated agreement and stated the Commission should add
program parameters.

Commissioner Skophammer stated the Commission should review donation
applicants or provide a bidding option.

Chair Villablanca suggested an annual review of the program.

The Commission unanimously recommended leaving the donation program at
seven years.

Community Services Director Riesgo requested that the Commission review and
provide feedback on the bench options that were removed following the Broad Fire.

Commissioner Peak suggested adding memorial plaques to existing benches and
picnic tables.

Commissioner Goldfarb suggested installing multiple plaques on a memorial
bench, rather than memorializing only one person.

The Commission recommended replacing the three damaged benches with a
concrete backless bench and establish a seven-year agreement with those donors.

In response to Commissioner Peak, Community Services Director Riesgo stated
staff would research municipal memorial programs.

Commissioner Goldfarb opposed adding more plaques to an existing memorial item
once the term ends.

Chair Villablanca opposed adding new park memorial benches.

Commissioner Peak indicated agreement with Chair Villablanca and stated
memorial rocks should also be removed.

The Commission recommended installing memorial plaques on the twelve existing
picnic tables at Malibu Bluffs Park.

In response to Commissioner Skophammer, Community Services Director Riesgo
stated ten people were on the Malibu Bluffs Park donor interest list.

Commissioner Goldfarb stated that the Commission should implement a simple and
fair process.
   Parks and Recreation Commission
  Regular Meeting
  Minutes of October 21, 2025
  Page 5 of 6

  Chair Villablanca stated the application should include residency information, age,
  the importance of the location, and the person’s connection to Malibu.

  The Commission recommended revisions to the allowable enhancements: l)
  Malibu Bluffs Park: remove memorial rock and bench donations; 2) All locations
  (excluding Malibu Bluffs Park): revising memorial rock donations to memorial
  plaque donations; 3) All locations (excluding Malibu Bluffs Park) revising bench
  donations to bench plaque donations; 4) Trancas Canyon Park: remove dog park
  shelter donation; 5) Malibu Senior Center: remove storage cart donation; 6) remove
  the Malibu Community Pool; and 7) Charmlee Wilderness Park: add bench plaque,
  picnic table plaque, tree donation without a plaque, and native plants.

  Commissioner Peak suggested that donors pay 50% of their initial donation to
  extend their memorial donation every 7 years beyond the original term.

  The Commission indicated agreement with Commissioner Peak.

MOTION  Chair Villablanca moved, and Commissioner Goldfarb seconded a motion to l)
  replace the three benches damaged during the Broad Fire with concrete backless
  benches; 2) approve the recommended revisions to the Park Enhancement and
  Donation Program; 3) include memorial plaque options on twelve existing picnic
  tables at Malibu Bluffs Park; 4) donation plaques would be $2,000; and 5) create a
  Commission Ad Hoc to annually review the Park Enhancement and Donation
  program, applications, and provide recommendations. The question was called, and
  the motion carried 4-0; Vice Chair Lingo absent.

ITEM 6  STAFF UPDATES

  Interim Recreation Manager Orosz provided an update on Charmlee Wildemess
  Park hikes and outdoor recreation programming.

  Community Services Director Riesgo provided an update on the Senior Center
  Resource Fair, Park Tales, Special Events, the Community Lands Project, Skate
  Park, Snack Shack, and Commission meeting schedule.

CONSENSUS By Consensus, the Commission unanimously agreed to cancel the December l6,
  2025, Regular meeting and conduct a Special Meeting at Malibu Bluffs Park on
  Tuesday, December 9, 2025, at 3:30 PM.

ITEM 7  COMMISSIONER REPORTS, COMMENTS AND INQUIRIES

  Commissioner Goldfarb stated she opposed the vegetation removal at Las Flores
  Creek Park (Rambla Pacifico Street).
